title: Trivial Adapters (The Identity Adapter)
pattern: An adapter struct that implements a target interface by delegating directly to a source interface that already has the matching signature.
why_bad: Adds zero value. If the interface signatures already match, adapting them is an identity operation that introduces boilerplate.
detection: An adapter struct implementing trait A by calling methods on an inner type that already implements trait A.
counterexample: Adapter translating between genuinely different traits or mismatching method signatures.
fix: Remove the adapter and let callers use the original type directly.
source: Joshua Kerievsky, *Refactoring to Patterns* (2004), Chapter 8 ("Generalization - Adapter"), p. 247.
